translation:
The bones are small and the flesh is tender, so this is certainly not the constitution of a pine or cypress. The pulse is rapid and the menses have ceased, so the signs of vacuity-exhaustion (虚劳) are already apparent. Since the congenital foundation is already weak and water is deficient, and the strong fire blazes again while metal dries up. Whenever the yearly qi completes one cycle there is one injury; how could it bear another injury? The autumn wind has already wounded it just as it begins to rise, so a grave injury can hardly be avoided. The pattern is as described above, and the medicinals only supplement the north (kidney). I do not dare call it a dream; I merely use this to allay sarcasm. [Medicinals] shengdi (Rehmanniae radix), shashen (Adenophorae/Glehniae radix), digupi (Lycii cortex), maidong (Ophiopogonis radix), jinshihu (Dendrobii caulis), sheng biejia (fresh turtle plastron).

Case of the tribute envoy of the Sulu Kingdom with prolonged cough who could not lie supine: Distinguishing the winds of the eight directions and surveying the natures of the five soils, by and large your honored country lies askew upon the xun (巽) direction of the Central Xia, before Jiwui (箕尾) and beyond Yizhen (翼轸), where the yang qi is excessively dispersed, so that even where there is wind-cold one catches it easily and scatters it easily. Having come to this Central China, it already belongs to the triple burner. All the more since one cannot lie down, the lung qi is greatly wounded, and one should only moisten and downbear. [Medicinals] honey-roasted pipaye (Eriobotryae folium), maidong, chuanbei (Fritillariae bulbus), sweet xingren (Seminis Armeniacae), frost-touched sangye (Mori folium), miren (Coicis semen).

The Inner Canon (《内経》) says: People with brittle bones and soft flesh have a naturally weak constitution. Yet comparing this by pulse and pattern, the cough originally belonged to the hand taiyin. I hear that the first physician supplemented, and the later physician drained, so that the pathogen was raised by the supplementation while the original qi was emptied by the draining, ending up as 'when the soldiers of the city go forth, the soldiers of the shore enter.' I also join the lowly opinion, sharing in one measure of amusement. [Medicinals] bei shashen, yanwo (swiftlet nest), sangye, bingtang (sugar), chuanbeimu, ziwan (Asteris radix).

In the lower abdomen a formed mass rises high like a mound, and when it reaches the region below the heart there is reversal (厥逆). It comes swiftly and departs even more swiftly, so that even a man of great strength cannot repel it. Upward it makes the body of the person vault upward, and downward it makes the body plummet, and one cannot forcibly endure it. With each closing and opening, each rising and falling, the person's whole body is moved up and down like a pestle in a mortar. The blood from the mouth, nose and the two yin orifices spills outward following its rise and fall, and the host of physicians cannot treat it. I think this pattern is recorded in the Classic of Difficult Issues (《難経》); it was only that it was not laid out in detail to show people. It also says: when this thing lies hidden beside the navel, above or below, the pain is a little reduced; when it lies hidden within the navel, one is a little more at ease. Thus one may see that the two points beside the navel also fit this item, but I shall not reveal its meaning, and let it be left for the assembled gentlemen to think through and obtain. [Medicinals] Send down the Shenmi wan (Mysterious Secret Pill) with a decoction of mint (薄荷). Because the patient thought that when drinking this decoction the thing would suddenly lie still and not move, it was therefore used.

Since the root has long been weakened and damaged, not only does the patient himself dislike it, but even those who wield the art of the physician find themselves in a position of being hobbled in front and behind. Encountering the season when wind-wood is at its height, the eyes became ill and turned yellow, and soon after there was seminal emission and dribbling turbid urine. After a short space, there was again swelling and pain of the knee and shin so that one could not walk. When he came for consultation, the pulse on the left was stringlike and rapid, on the right bounding and long; the face was deep purple and he vomited from time to time. Quietly reflecting on the cause, the numerous previous illnesses were all one and the same pathogen, which became three diseases that entangled one another in succession. From above going down, and from below reaching the extreme lower part, because the body had long had its root pulled away, it steamed upward again to become a stomach disease; this is because the kidney and stomach are mutually related. If one does not somewhat reduce and remove one or two [of these], but only takes to returning yang and restoring the root, I privately fear that like the swordgate stubbornly refusing, the yin-steadiness would not again be the possession of Han. I respectfully plan one method, slightly following Danxi; I know not how it will fare. [Medicinals] lingyangjiao (Saigae cornu), mugua (Chaenomelis fructus), wine-fried huangbai (Phellodendri cortex), fulonggan (Terra flava usta), sheng miren, juhong (Citri exocarpium rubrum), maliaodou (Viciae fabae semen).

The wasting illness (癘) being cured is like the horn of the qilin and the horn of the rabbit. If one perhaps knocks at the jade terrace and the cinnabar gate, seeking a single golden leaf, one will almost feel pleased and enlightened. [Medicinals] Xiao jianzhong tang (Minor Constructing the Middle Decoction).

The pulse of the right three positions shows surging, rapid, stringlike and tense together, while the left upper is rapid and the middle tense. First one had the disease of yang essence not ascending, and next this reached yang collaterals not being firm. For the extreme yin engendering yang, not guarding [essence] and losing essence is the congenital; while the extreme yang issuing from yin, failing in what is hidden and spitting blood is the postnatal. This is to say that after the formed body first began, the congenital and postnatal are again both diseased. Even a body of consummate genuine surplus would not suffice to supply this gradual consumption. Now shall I use things of heavy flavor that enter yin? Or shall I use those of thin flavor that are clear yang? I privately fear that the mountains, rivers, plants and trees all cannot suffice to return the metal-graded product. I only long for a great medicinal and a golden elixir, the firing schedule of the circulating heaven. Yet I cannot help but also supplement with a formula for taking as food. I plan to await the honored master to fix the same; in the end I am ashamed of beating a cloth drum. I hope for his indulgence. [Medicinals] Jian lianrou (Nelumbinis semen, one catty; keeping the kernel, pounding it to the size of sesame, steaming over rice and drying nine times, then making into powder), maidongrou (one catty), young heye (half a catty), ding shengdi (Rehmanniae radix, four liang), jinyingzi (Rosae laevigatae fructus, half a catty, removing the hairs).

Simmer the above four medicinals into an ointment and pound together with the lotus seed powder into pills; send down five qian with a decoction of qiushi (autumnal stone salt).

Depressed and frustrated, sad and bored, the heart thus becomes biased and askew, and when the twelve officials all lose their ruler, then the yin qi conjoins with the yang qi. Administer a heavy settling formula. [Medicinals] sheng tieluo (iron filings), yujin (Curcumae radix), banxia (Pinelliae rhizoma), kushen (Sophorae radix), juhong (Citri exocarpium rubrum), fuling (Poria).

Yang reaches its extreme and ascends without entering, while yin is depressed and sinks without clinging; this is why there is day but no night, and the bright sun sleeps at noon, and water gradually declines. Treat by crossing yin and yang, guiding the defensive to enter the constructive. Do not say that a blood-condition forbids banxia. [Medicinals] banxia, suanzaoren (Ziziphi spinosae semen), shengdi, sheng gancao (fresh licorice), nuomi (glutinous rice), fuling, miren, qu you ruxiang (frankincense, oil removed).

This is summer heat seasonal pathogen, and the illness has lasted twenty days. Since every method has already been exhausted, why raise the question of the road to a lame-footed one? Having been invited to come through the heat, I reluctantly sweat and compose a formula. [Medicinals] chuanlian (Coptidis rhizoma), banxia, sheng gancao, danqin (Scutellariae radix), fuling, shengjiang (ginger).

This pattern arose originally from the stomach lacking its harmonious (沖和) qi. In short, the harmonious qi is the original qi of great harmony. To give position to heaven and earth and to nurture the ten thousand things is none other than this qi. Even a slight insufficiency is already not appropriate; how much more when it is greatly injured. In my humble view one should reject everything, nurture oneself loftily in a mountain study, feed on medicinals and minerals, and stand freely beyond the world; then one will almost recover. If one remains wielding the brush in the lotus-curtained (counselor's) tent, it is not appropriate. I have heard that the gentleman gives to others through words and loves others through virtue; therefore I have gone on at length even to these trivialities. [Medicinals] xuanfuhua (Inulae flos), mugua, sheng guyan (dried sprouted rice), zhi gancao (honey-roasted licorice), daizheshi (haematite), baishao (Paeoniae radix alba), nuomizhi (glutinous rice juice).

After the festival the illness worsened, and many physicians were experienced in turn. In the morning Mr. Zhang spoke of heat, in the evening Mr. Li spoke of cold. The viscera and bowels each have what they receive and contain, and the movements of qi each have their opening and closing. As a single indistinct body tasting throughout both supplementation and draining, one is liable to become ill even without being ill. One should hold to the correct and maintain the method; take care not to delight in grand achievements. [Medicinals] Danggui jianzhong tang (Tanggui-Fortified Constructing the Middle Decoction).

The pulse is stringlike and tense as if following the edge of a blade, without the least harmonious qi. The water qi is excessive and the metal order does not reach it. What comes from behind is called the oppressive overcoming. If one does not truly bring about the qi of great harmony to dissolve the perverse and discordant, it will inevitably come to the point where yin loses its concealment and yang has nothing to lean upon. 'When you tread on frost, the solid ice is sure to come'—how could one not take precautions before the rain? Laozi says: 'When the teeth are hard they snap'—that is roughly it. I admonish again and again. Keep this formula, expecting to win the pledge. [Medicinals] zhi gancao, bei shashen, liaodoupi, dong sangye (winter mulberry leaf), sheng baishao, maidongrou.

The central earth, by its lofty height, fixes the positions of the eight directions, and so Shu lies in kun (坤). One who is nurtured in this region should have a pulse that is moderate and fluent. Now the bounding-surge is excessive and the face is yellow with heavy qi; fortunately one has long lived in Zhe; if one were in the native home, this pulse-pattern would bring blood spilling. Now that he is returning to Shu, he should take pills early to nourish it. [Medicinals] Liuwei dihuang wan (Six-Ingredient Rehmannia Pill).

The pulses of the pure and honored are mostly the six yang, next the six yin; these are all pure and unalloyed signs. Now the body being endowed with the six yang is one manifestation. The breath is divided into the nine indicators, and the positions into the three sections. Although within a single section all the viscera are examined, the one that clearly stands out in the left section is the three viscera of heart, liver, kidney. Now at the inch it is vacant and large: this is the heart not concealing the spirit. The gate pulse is slippery and rapid: this is wood without the nourishment of water. At the foot it is floating and large: this is the water qi not being leveled. Fire takes wood as its body, and wood takes water as its mother; the congenital single qi thereby becomes luminous and clear. Therefore one knows that in the li hexagram the even line engenders yin, and the heart qi daily wishes to descend and mix; while in the kan hexagram the odd line engenders yang, and the kidney qi daily wishes to ascend and carry on. This is the single crossing of heart and kidney. The Dan formula says: 'When water and fire mix one never ages'—this is what is meant. There is nothing more than, amid the ordinary daily rounds, the heart desiring calm, the liver desiring harmony, and the kidney desiring fullness. Only then will there be no trance and palpitation, nor numbness of the four limbs, and the four limbs will be at ease. Respectfully I lay out one formula first nourishing the constructive and defensive. As for the method of nurturing, I shall seek again to lay out a diagram. [Medicinals] renshen (ginseng), zaoren (Ziziphi spinosae semen), yuanzhi (Polygalae radix), danggui, zhi gancao, shudi (cooked Rehmannia), fushen (Poria cum radice pini), yuanshen (Scrophulariae radix), baishao, muxiang (Saussureae radix).

The pulse-pattern is somewhat more harmonized than before, and the two hands are level, both having returned to the substance of the six yang, so one may prognosticate that there is no qi from without; only the constructive and defensive are slightly vacuous. But seeing that the registers and documents are pressing and various, the heart yin must be cultured and the kidney yang must be concealed, so as to supply the daily spirit and to match the sovereign's will as one governs the people. First prepare the decoction to take into the provincial capital, taking one dose daily to build up and supplement; then follow with ointment and pills in succession. The spirit of your honor's body will naturally daily reach vigor and ease. [Medicinals] renshen, zaoren, guishen (Tangkuei, body part), zhi gancao, fushen, yuanshen, baishao, gouqi (Lycii fructus), cooked hutaoren (Seminis Juglandis), guiyuanrou (longan flesh).

When the Inner Canon (《内経》) speaks of the binding of the three yang forming the diaphragm (膈), it refers only to the taiyang, yangming and shaoyang. Now compared by pulse and complexion, the shaoyin and jueyin are also diseased. Taking the filling and supplementing of the lower burner as the foremost task is admittedly proper, but the one part that is the stomach-gate—by what path does it fly across? Moreover there is a ball of depressed fire that, carrying the wood pathogen, rushes horizontally and arrogantly in the central burner; obtaining heat as its companion it becomes ever more rampant. Bitter and cold is not permitted by the circumstances, while sweet and cold cannot be delayed. If the lung does not engender fluids and the large intestine does not engender liquids, then the fluids become ever more depleted and the illness ever more numerous. Moreover what rushes upward is the liver pathogen; it is that water does not engender it. What does not accept is a stomach disease; it is that the lung qi does not descend. Within the single body, fluids and the essence are all of the utmost importance. In my unworthy view, I devote myself to this; I know not what to make of it. First present the Five-Juice Drink (五汁飲), then it will do to discuss the administration of medicinals. [Medicinals] lugen (Phragmitis rhizoma juice), ganzhe (sugarcane juice), maogen (Imperatae rhizoma juice), xian ou (fresh lotus root juice), shuili (water pear juice), one cup each; shengjiang juice and chenxiang juice, one small spoon each.

On examination, the pulse shows only thin and weak with vacuity, and the stringlike pattern has entirely withdrawn. The hands and feet tremble and shake: this is a sign of the original qi being depleted and weakened. The reason the previously administered medicinals all had little effect is that the original qi could not carry the medicinals to move their orders. Now if the original qi does not recover in a day, the disease course does not retreat in a day. The disease course and the original qi are not originally set side by side—this one growing and that one vanishing is the constant of principle. In my humble view the decoction is of secondary importance; one must take medicinals that go straight to the congenital as pastes and pills, taken morning and evening, and over time they will naturally suffice. When the original qi and original essence recover in one morning, the postnatal food and drink become strong by themselves without being forced. Because this pattern is not one of sudden contraction or internal injury, there is no need to repeatedly change the formula, which would injure the appetite of the yangming stomach. And does not the Canon say: 'that which adapts to the stomach is supplementation'? For decoction taken long—does it or does it not adapt to the stomach? I, from Wuzhong, accepting the order of His Honor the Remonstrance official (給諫公), have come here to diagnose the complexion and pulse once, and surely know it does not depart from this principle. I have reluctantly stayed for the General (鎮台) three days, first out of gratitude for the General's lowered condescension to a scholar, and second for the Remonstrance official's deep affection for a kinsman, and to let the physicians of Zhe seek out a gap and open a hollow in return to the General. Now, having weighed the pulse and pattern, do not engage in revision, and directly supplement the congenital. I propose presenting the three formulas of decoction, paste, and pill. Use the decoction for the moment; take the paste frequently from time to time; and make the pill the fixed [regimen] at daybreak. After more than twenty days of filling and supplementing there will be news. Should I still knock at the steps to re-examine? (The formulas are not seen.)

Your honor's body is originally yin vacuous, and the yang qi issues alone together with the pathogen, the heat persisting more than twenty days without resolving. This is because the yin fluids are dried up and cannot produce sweat, so the pathogen also does not resolve. After successive doses that nurture yin, when the pathogen relaxes a little, then a great sweat is vented; this is the time of clouds traveling and rain bestowing, all things enjoying full efficacy—how could one doubt that it is desertion? But when a weak body has long been ill without resolution and the original qi is ever more depleted, this slight emergence of the pathogen and production of a great sweat also belongs to the crucial moment of receiving and supplementing, and one may not be lax for a moment. If the heart is calm, then the qi settles and the spirit abides. Be absolutely sure not to worry and agitate the spirit-qi, causing the yang qi to ascend. In utmost admonishment I say this again. [Medicinals] renshen four qian, shudi one liang, baomu fushen two qian, tiandong (Asparagi radix) three qian, zhi shouwu (prepared Polygoni multiflori radix) five qian, zuo gumuli (left-facing Ostrea testa) six qian.

The pulse is vacant, empty and stringlike; there is urgent pain in the abdomen: it is a liver disease. If treating the liver does not respond, treating the spleen is also a fine method. [Medicinals] cu guizhi (coarse cinnamon twig) one qian, moyao (myrrh) five fen, baishao two qian (stir-fried yellow), gancao one qian (stir-fried black), hupo (amber) one qian, yitang (maltose) one and a half qian.

The bones are small and the flesh tender—not originally the constitution of pine or cypress; mixing hot, cold, supplemental and draining in a jumble—how is this a life-preserving art? Fortunately one eats well and the stools are firm, so one may yet be supported through the autumn. But the sinews of the calves are broken and the flesh fallen, one sleeps on one's side with the menses obstructed, and the physician still remains in a daze—why? I am old and do not speak of medicine; I merely write a few words and plan one formula. [Medicinals] shudi, zhi gancao, danggui, sheng zuo gumuli (fresh left oyster shell).

The twelve channels all have cough; how could a stomach disease fail to have cough? All the more when this earth is diseased in the metal viscus and the bowel is also diseased. Seeking then, in this, one's pain and diarrhea—one lies in the upper stomach duct and one lies in the large intestine (the bowel of the lung)—so that one has nowhere to trace their course. Lifting the head to plan in the chamber, one must divide the soldiers and join in the surrounding assault. Only then do I plan one method, which I ask the senior physicians to refine; if thereby one may benefit its refinement, perhaps even a lowly word may be worth gathering, like the effort of a shrimp moving a boat. [Medicinals] Jiangxi chishizhi (terra Flava usta) six liang (calcined), stir-fried black ganjiang (dried ginger) one liang. Grind the two medicinals into powder and form pills with yellow rice (huangmi).

renshen one qian, zhi-hei gancao one qian, dazao (jujube) five qian, yitang five qian, guimu (cinnamon) one qian, wine-fried baishao two qian, roaste-ripe shengjiang one qian. Decoct once in water, remove the dregs, and send down the aforementioned Taohua wan (Peach-Blossom Pill) three qian.

The disease is originally damp-warmth, and the original qi cannot carry the pathogen out, so it has a tendency to directly invade the central burner. I plan to separate open the zhi-zi and douchi above and below, to raise and lower the ginger and qin (Scutellaria) left and right, and to dissolve with fragrant herbs across, hoping to sweep clear the various pathogens. I know not whether one may gain success of the skin and meridian. [Medicinals] hei shanzhi (Gardeniae fructus), danqin, chuan yujin (Curcumae radix), sheng xiangfu (Cyperi rhizoma), chao-xiang douchi (fermented soybean), shengjiang, xian shichangpu (Acori graminei rhizoma, fresh), sheng gancao.

The illness has been long and its threads are disordered, but in the end it does not leave the single viscus of jueyin. Now I plan to use the supporting metal qi to secretly control it, to soothe and pacify it with qi that nourishes the constructive, and to solidify the taiyin to block and resist it. This also is the intent of Zigong preserving Lu and of Yue overthrowing Wu. [Medicinals] lingyangjiao, renshen, zhi shouwu, qing ejiao (equine glue), maidong, yun fushen (Poria cum radice pini).

On examination, the genuine qi has long not circulated through the four limbs, and moreover there is a sudden contraction of summer-heat pathogen of the wind-stroke (類中) type. There is enuresis and the eyes are closed; the pulse is stringlike and rapid and ascends to obtain fish border (魚際). Wind of the liver is of the foot jueyin, and wind of summer heat is of the hand jueyin; when the two channels of hand and foot are both diseased and one is mute and unable to speak, it is incurable. Moreover move to a nearby cool place as a sickroom, and externally resolve the summer-heat pathogen while internally using a formula that matches the pattern to rescue the reversal. [Medicinals] lingyangjiao, zhuru (Bambusae caulis in taeniam), lianqiaoren (Forsythiae fructus), xian sangzhi (fresh mulberry twig), banxia, xian shichangpugen (fresh Acorus rhizome).

In human life at fifty one viscus declines; how much more approaching sixty? What the assembled disputants contend over all centers on the kidney. Because, as was stated, the great intention is to grip and hold the spleen-earth; then the pivot is obtained and the four movements are accomplished. [Medicinals] Duzhu gao (Single Atractylodes Paste), first using ten catties will do.

The genuine qi is already exhausted; how could the illness be cured? He who has a method to cure it must be an immortal. [Medicinals] Gui-shao liujun [tang] without gancao, with fresh sangzhi decoction as water in its place.

This is a case where the taiyin is steamed and fumigated by dampness, having lost its power of clear purification, and wood has nothing to fear, so the right shoulder and arm increasingly show a pattern of non-movement (不仁). The wine leaven (麴糵) injures one's life, and yet one still delights in it—this I do not understand. [Medicinals] sheng miren, xian lugen, shengdi, nen sangzhi, bai guishen, chishao (peony, red).

In the human body the channels run from the chest to the hands, and from the abdomen to the feet, eighty zhang (丈) surrounding and reaching to the whole body. There is never one whose sinews are injured by hidden cold and yet does not reach downward; though the first and later times differ, the harm they cause is one. Without Bao Gu's moxa and Wen Bo's needle it cannot be cured. One may internally take Batang (Eight-Ingredient Decoction). [Medicinals] Guifu bawei wan (Cinnamon and Aconite Eight-Ingredient Pill).

People of fawning and flattery often have cravings, and people of accumulated depression often have fire. Over a long time, the pent-up and depressed disposition bursts forth like a wild wind and overturning waves, as if mad, as if enchanted. Since medicinals and minerals can no longer be given, first burn cinnabar medicines in the room to repel the madness and perversity. [Medicinals] Ruyi dan (As-You-Wish Elixir) seven pills.

The beard and eyebrows fall on their own, the skin and hair are moist and glossy, and the pulse comes floating and uneven: this is wind, not graying and whitening with age. The thirty-six kinds issue from the same source but differ in name; this is not a shallow ailment. In summer one should eat xiangfeng she (fragrant-wind snake, i.e., the commonly called black-wind snake), cooked together with chicken. [Medicinals] bai guishen, baima (Hemp), chishao, shengdi, zaoliangcao (Ecliptae herba), jiangcan (Bombyx batryticatus), yinhua (honeysuckle flower), chongweizi (Leonuri fructus), xiakucao (Prunellae spica).

That in headache one cannot see people when gazing into the dark is the first contraindication; that liver wind vomits the bile is the second contraindication. Having been companions for years, the only intimate is this one person; how could one sit and watch? One must strive to win him back, and yet there is a certain destiny at work in the state. [Medicinals] Ju dan-tang (Bile-Warming Decoction 沮膽湯) without zhishi, adding tianma (Gastrodiae rhizoma), gouteng (Uncariae ramulus), and sangye.

This pattern is after all liver wind; then the single channel of jueyin is not easy to control. In the ancient method there is a technique of settling and restraining, and a technique of cultivating the earth to resist. Therefore Dongyuan has his Banzia Tianma tang (Pinellia and Gastrodia Decoction), and Jingyue also composed the Zuogui Yin to make up for its omissions. Now neither of the two methods can be used purely, so I plan a mixed formula to be held for selection. [Medicinals] renshen, jiao zhu (fried Atractylodis rhizoma), fuling, baiziren (Platycladi semen), banxia, chenpi (tangerine peel), shudi, bai guishen, zhi gancao, biejia (turtle plastron).

Prolonged cough shifts the pathogen to invade the stomach; because of the cough the lung has lost its power of purifying and downbearing, so the qi rises and rebels. Do not use medicinals that drain and injure the lung qi. [Medicinals] Take a pear, remove the core but keep the peel, pound it into a pulp, filter through silk, slowly boil over a gentle fire into a paste, store it in a porcelain jar and seal the mouth with wax. Daily send down five qian with boiled water.

The yangming pulse is replete; the qi is urgent and wheezing; the strong fire eats the qi, melting away the genuine yin. It is severe when the summer qi unfurls, and is an even plain at the time of stripping dates. At this moment one cannot make other plans; for now give Wendan tang (Warming the Gallbladder Decoction) to somewhat abate the heat and protect the wounded metal. Wendan tang.

A person of abundant body must have weak qi. When cold and heat suddenly arise, there immediately appear scant and rapid urine, shaking of the head and neck, dry tongue and parched teeth, hurried qi, and a pulse that is left stringlike and right weak, thirsting but not desiring to drink. These all are signs of the original [qi] not overcoming the pathogen. I fear that, taking advantage of the decline of their fluids, it will suddenly sink inward; one should cautiously ponder and weigh, for at this very moment the dryness order is in force. [Medicinals] tianhuafen (Trichosanthis radix), juan zhuye (Lophatheri herb), hou juhong, qinghao (Artemisiae annuae herba), maidong, liuyisan (Six-to-One Powder).

The pulse is rapid; for five or six days one has not changed clothes (not had bowel movement); the tongue is yellow and the lips scorched. The stomach heat is blazing. Moreover the previously taken medicinals are all pungent-warm medicinals that consume yin, so now nothing but cold and cooling will do. Yet one should attend carefully and make protection the chief concern, because the heat pathogen has deeply entered yin and the yang qi alone is in excess. [Medicinals] chuan huanglian, zhishi, gualou (Trichosanthis fructus), chishao, sheng gancao, chenpi, xingren, mutong (Akebiae caulis).

The origin of the illness arose from eating too much persimmon and catching cold. It has now been more than twenty years. Understand that the persimmon is a tree of the west, and its fruit is formed by receiving the qi of autumn metal; one can know that because it seeks kind with the lung metal, its pathogen enters the lung and issues as qi-type asthma, and over time the kidney water loses its root and, being vacuous, overflows upward to become phlegm. The stomach is the vessel that stores phlegm, so the Jiangqi tang and Liujunzi tang, going from the lung to the stomach, both obtain a small effect. But what does not eliminate the root—just as if one does not uproot Ju, the earth of Qi will in the end not be a possession of Yan—especially as the pulse-pattern is still fierce; one should penetrate deeply into the site of disease. I plan the method of Zhongjing. [Medicinals] tian tingli (descurainiae semen, sweet), ku tingli (bitter tingli), dazao.

Coughing with loss of blood has already exceeded three years, lingering without end; the color is dark and the pulse stringlike, the cough ever more severe, and the mouth rim is yellow. Proceeding from the liver and spleen, and reaching the kidney, the upper storehouse becomes what is drawn on for its demands and can no longer respond. The drink also thereby becomes a misfortune; one cannot expel it, and nourishing it has no merit. Delaying and daily wasting, it cannot be remedied. One should take the center of it to hope for its spread and circulation; perhaps that is near. I pattern on the Constructing-the-Middle (建中) method, adding phlegm-washing medicinals; having waited for the yangming to ascend and then following with great supplementation of the taiyin, one gradually enters the pure-yin method; otherwise it is not treatment. [Medicinals] Xiao jianzhong tang without ginger, adding fuling and jiangpi.

When the ancients created the character, two fires exerting force make "labor" (勞), so it is spoken of for the sovereign and minister fires. One warms and supplements the central burner to quiet the source of phlegm, and supplements the lower burner to increase the source of water. But the disease has already reached a depth that, I fear, a single blow cannot break open. [Medicinals] shudi, gouqizi, yuanshen, niuxi (Achyranthis radix), fuling, zishiying (fluorite).

Lying horizontally it becomes the three kan (坎) lines, and standing upright it becomes the water of a river (川水); the single point of true yang in the middle, when water is deficient, becomes exposed as the dragon fire; when it moves it is Zhen (震), and the yang below Zhen shares the same source with it, ascending to become thunder fire; this is why thunder belongs to wood—all are fires within yin. Pure-yin medicinals, the more one pours them on, the more they blaze, and no plant or tree can control it. One should use the Yiyuan elixir (一元丹), and take it long to be cured. [Medicinals] dan qiushi (crystal autumn stone salt) five or six catties, made into pills with boiled and mashed red dates. Take five or six qian in the morning and two or three qian in the evening, sending down with a little yang qiushi (yang autumn stone salt) dissolved in hot water.

The pulse is stringlike and rapid, the foot position alone is large, and there is cough with sore throat and loss of voice. After the loss of blood of several years, that the yin is deficient and the fire blazes need hardly be spoken. Only a supremely still medicament drawing yang to submerge into yin would approach the intent of the Inner Canon (《内経》). Yet one must practice a static cultivation effort, making yin secret and yang guarded, and gaining the power of kan and li mutually crossing is best. [Medicinals] shudi, haishi (shell powder, pounded), jinshihu, bei shashen, fuling, maimendong, sheng baishao, gui (turtle) abdominal plate, shanyao (Dioscoreae rhizoma).

The body suddenly and gradually thins, the pulse is extremely vacuous, the qi is timid with occasional cough, the eyes dark and the pulse stringlike, and one is suddenly unhappy. Supplementing qi and supplementing blood is what everyone knows; one should draw a yin beast into the yin to make the medicinals all the more potent. Morning and evening catch one otter, take the liver and dry it in the shade, and with deer-horn glue pound each into powder in wooden vessels. Take one qian of deer-horn glue powder in the morning and one qian of otter-liver powder in the evening, both sent down with boiled water. This is the method commonly used for a hundred days; now plan the decoction formula to take first. [Medicinals] renshen, fuling, tusiban (Semen Cuscutae cake), nanzao, jiao dongzhu (fried Atractylodes), zhi gancao, gouqizi.

The left gate pulses with vigor pressing the finger, urgent and swift, and the right gate is stringlike and large. There is no failure of the stomach qi to return to the source; the full sea has no root. If the right gate is as such, it should be severe in spring; if the left gate is as such, it should snap in autumn. I fear the left gate is its response, so reluctantly I plan the yiji-tongyuan (乙癸同源) treatment of the ancients. [Medicinals] da shengdi, nvzhenzi (Ligustri fructus), gouqizi, fushen, yuanshen, huai shanyao, zishiying.

This illness arose from overtaxing the mind and wearying toil, with wind and cold not being tempered, until there came coughing and spitting phlegm which over a long time became internal injury. Internal injury means injury to the qi of the inner viscera—that is what the ancients called the vacuity-labor pattern (虚劳), which in general is not cured. One must cut off the affairs that overexert the mind and weary with toil, not letting up a single hair of any worldly thought, and assist with medicinals; then perhaps one may prolong the years. [Medicinals] maidong, ejiao, jiegeng (Platycodonis radix), zhi gancao, shashen, miren, fuling.

This is sha-labor (痧労). Arising from injury to the taiyin that daily transmits to the foot shaoyin. When the spleen qi slightly becomes loose, then it enters the lower storehouse. Of a hundred there is not one cure; one should quickly turn the boat around and go back, close the gates and rest quietly. Offer one formula as a gift; take it daily if you will. [Medicinals] shudi, ejiao, baihe (Lilii bulbus), gouqizi.

For a person of sixty years (花甲), the two foot positions are alone large. At a time when the two viscera have already declined, is this appropriate? Quickly advance the yiji-tongyuan method. [Medicinals] shudi, nvzhenzi, tusiban, fuling, yuanshen, zaoliangcao (Ecliptae herba), gouqizi. Make with honey into pills.

This is a genuine yin deficiency pattern, vulgarly called the hundred-day labor (百日労). Having a little hidden summer-heat, the shivering and heat become ever more severe thereby. It is a pity that it was not treated early. [Medicinals] shudi, qiancao (Rubiae radix), qinghao, yuanshen, huashi (Talcum), danpi (Moutan cortex).

In the kan hexagram one line's true yang flies alone above; once it meets the months of si and wu (of fire), even the divine water and golden elixir can do nothing with it. [Medicinals] old shengjiang, tiandong, huai niuxi, gancao, chuan shihu, yuanshen, nvzhenzi.

By natural disposition this person is fond of eating pungent things; the medical books say: 'eating much pungent [food] causes sudden death.' Now, having examined that the complexion, pulse, frame and body of flesh are all exhausted, without waiting for sudden death, neither will he be long-lived. Naturally he should keep hold of his illness. First cause him to take the Sansheng yin (Three-Life Drink). [Medicinals] sheng dihuang, chi fuling (Poria, red), maidong, fen gancao, sheng miren, hongzao.

This is a single depletion pattern (損證), one that depletes downward from above. First deplete the lung; the lung again transmits to the heart, transmits to the liver, transmits to the spleen, and reaches the kidney, then the bones wilt and one cannot lie in bed. One absolutely must not again administer lung-regulating [medicinals] to hasten the depletion. One may take the Pa Zhudou Wan (Bitter-Pork-Stomach Pill 怕豬肚丸). [Medicinals] Pa zhudou wan.

Before reaching fifty years, the form, pulse and complexion are all declined. When asked, he had successively lost three sons. How could it not be as such? And how much more when he has also grieved over his grandsons? This is not something that medicinals and food can accomplish. [Medicinals] chuanbeimu, shengdi, fuling, maidong.

One obtains a pulse that is rapid and moreover stringlike. This is a yin deficiency pattern, not an external contraction. Now, as vacuity fire rises as headache, there gradually comes a tendency of both metal and water being wounded. Only quiet cultivation obtains it; medicinals and food are secondary. shudi, nvzhenzi, maidong, guiban (turtle plastron), yuanshen, dan qiushi. Make into pills with jujube puree and send down with boiled water.
translator_notes: 'Supplementing the north (補北)' is a euphemism for supplementing the kidney.
The Sulu Kingdom tribute envoy is identified as the speaker/subject.
'When the soldiers of the city go forth, the soldiers of the shore enter' is a metaphor that supplementing actually admitted the pathogen; translated literally.
'䐃' refers to calf/sinew flesh; kept per the source text.
沮膽湯 is kept as in the source text; it may be a misreading for 溫膽湯, but translated literally.
Formula names, medicinal names, acupoints, and dosages (jin, liang, qian, fen, cup, spoon) were rendered in standard TCM English terms without rounding or omission.
No modern disease or pathophysiological explanations were added; literal translation prioritized.
Bracketed notes and medicinal enumerations were preserved in parentheses.
Traditional preparation terms (秋石, 澹秋石, 陽秋石, 陰秋石) retained per pinyin reading.
The several case records joined under 一瓢醫案 within one source line were translated as a single part per the line-boundary-first rule.
Antithetical/parallel prose structures were not expanded into plain prose.
